display.title: Episode 124: The Rambam's Resting Place, Chapter 1 (Lag BaOmer)
display.summary_short: The show before Lag BaOmer: a twelve pesukim contest, Shema with a kindergartener, the life of the Rambam and the mystery of where he would be buried, and the day of Rashbi's joy.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the Tuesday before Lag BaOmer 5744. Uncle Yossi reminds listeners of the Lag BaOmer parade and the twelve pesukim signs on Eastern Parkway, and announces a contest: write in with the best time to say the twelve pesukim, such as waiting for the school bus, to win his new tape. He introduces the Rambam, explaining his name and the saying 'from Moshe to Moshe there arose none like Moshe'. A kindergartener recites the Shema. The story traces the Rambam's life: born in Cordova on Erev Pesach, forced to flee as a boy, wandering for years, saved from a storm at sea on the way to Eretz Yisroel, praying at the Kosel and in Chevron, and finally settling in Egypt, where he wrote his famous works. Before he passed away he asked to be buried in Eretz Yisroel without saying where, and the people of Yerushalayim, Chevron and Meron each claimed the honor. The chapter ends as a mysterious sign is about to reveal the answer. A listener's letter, a talk on Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and Lag BaOmer, parade bus details and the new tape close the show.
display.lesson: The Rambam held on to Torah and mitzvos through years of wandering; the answer to where he would rest comes next week.

date.note: 'May the 20th, this coming Sunday' is Lag BaOmer 5744; the Tuesday before.

advisories.note: The Rambam's family must flee Cordova and wander for years because they were not allowed to live as Jews.
